pr.title: feat(review-panel): pin reviewer effort and tools as data and bound a dying run's recovery [9k9.408]

work_item.gloss: predictable reviewer settings, as an interim cost control

summary: The agent running a review round used to choose each reviewer's effort and tools itself. The panel's configuration file now holds both for every reviewer slot. Every reviewer receives the change as a diff file. A run that dies follows a fixed recovery sequence. The panel does not yet check that a run actually used its pinned effort.
heads_up: The gates ran with the system bash first on PATH, because the Homebrew bash hangs one hook test.
The code reviewers last judged commit e399db1d, and five prose-only commits followed it.
The 27 raw answers that test the written dispatch rules are outside the repository.

changes.text: contracts.json pins effort and tools for every reviewer slot, and no reviewer gets a shell.
The emitter writes one diff file beside each prompt.
A run that died is retried one effort step lower, then on the other provider. The round halts after three attempts.

design_notes:
The earlier design routed the OpenRouter mid-tier model away from whole-document reads. That constraint had no run record behind it, and the only recorded reads of that shape on that model had finished. A constraint stated without its variables cannot be scoped or falsified, so the design no longer encodes it. A slot that names a model runs that model. The recovery sequence answers for a death when one happens, and records every attempt. During this pull request's own review that model finished 20 whole-document reads in 20.

Rejected: letting the dispatcher pick a fallback model freely. That hides the cost decision in a prompt and leaves no record. Rejected: a shell grant restricted by a command prefix. Both `git diff` and `git log` accept `--output`, so a prefix pattern is not read-only.

contracts.json holds eight slots by provider, tier and read scope, plus the staffing recommender and the trend checkpoint. OpenRouter reads a whole document at low effort and a diff at high. Codex frontier slots run at high and mid slots at medium. No pin names a model, because the routing table does that. Every tool grant is the Codex read-only sandbox, or a list drawn from Read, Grep and Glob. No reviewer gets a shell pattern, because `git diff --output=<path>` writes a file.

The emitter writes each diff file over that reviewer's scope for the round, so a reviewer with no shell can still read the change. Reviewers sharing a revision pair share one computed diff. Each reviewer entry in the round record gains effort and tools copied from its pin. A slot with no pin refuses the round and writes nothing.

Each artifact class keeps exactly one OpenRouter reviewer. Four reviewers move to Codex. Declared tiers do not change.

The gate's claim command takes `--effort` and records it. A run that died may be claimed again only as the same model one effort step lower, or as the other provider at the same tier and scope. Anything else is refused and costs no attempt. After three attempts the round halts with guidance. A revert restarts a round in flight, because its attempts ledger gained a field.

harvest.md states the sequence, the failover slot, the diff file and the claim form. Nine scenarios with expected answers check that a reader holding only those files reaches the right dispatch.

The criteria attack panel needs the same pins, as slice B of this work item, and it is a different skill with its own configuration file. This pull request reshaped the claim record that #774 (the read-evidence gate) adds two fields to. That pull request's gate checks that a reviewer read what it was handed, and this one only hands it over.

The round record copies each pin, and tests check that too. This pull request's own first round ran every reviewer at its pin, on two vendors, with no substitution. Both recovery failures were real bugs found in review, reproduced, and fixed with a failing-then-passing test each. A stuck round also costs coverage, because it can look finished with one reviewer never having read the change.

The written doctrine could send whoever runs a round by hand down the wrong path. Nine written situations were answered by a model given only the doctrine files, and all 27 answers, three runs each, matched the expected dispatch. A reviewer without a shell could miss the change if its diff file were missing or covered the wrong scope. Tests cover the diff file's content, an empty change and an unknown revision, and a diff git cannot compute refuses the round before anything is dispatched.

findings.claim: The `Bash(git diff *)` and `Bash(git log *)` grants pinned for every OpenRouter lens are not read-only: both commands accept `--output=<path>`, which writes the diff to an arbitrary file, and the prefix pattern also matches invocations with shell redirection (`git diff <a> <b> > <path>`). A seat granted these patterns can write attacker-influenced bytes to any user-writable path despite the change's stated trust boundary that a reviewer's run is never able to write.

The tests can accept a Codex lens using its re-review tier for a whole-artifact read. Add an independent tier assertion for architectural-fit, which declares frontier and re-review mid, across the full-read scenarios.

The tier tests still describe re-review pricing as a consequence of the round number. The docstring saying “Round 2 resolves the declared re_review_tier” omits the delta-scope condition, and the new test name saying OpenRouter “rereads at mid” reinforces that misreading. Full rereads retain the declared tier in every round.
A fourth dead-run claim can bypass the exhaustion handler. It returns off-ladder, incorrectly says a failover is still accepted, omits halt guidance, and leaves the final failure unrecorded.
findings.reason: Reproduced: a fourth dead-run claim after initial/high, dead-run/medium, transport-error/medium on codex returned off-ladder with no halt block and no refusal ledger entry. Test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestDeadRunLadder::test_a17_a_dead_run_past_the_bound_is_out_of_attempts_not_off_ladder failed without the change (got ['off-ladder']) and passes with it; a mutant restoring the unconditional off-ladder raise was observed to fail only this test. Fix: claim() raises an off-ladder refusal only below MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a claim past the bound meets the bound's attempts-exhausted refusal with halt guidance and a refusal ledger record. Commit 75bb090c.

findings.claim: A dead run on the failover seat loses halt guidance when an earlier attempt returned unusable output. The dispatcher consequently receives a refusal that closes only the lens instead of halting the round.
findings.reason: Reproduced: initial codex, transport-error to openrouter, unusable-output on openrouter, then a dead-run claim on openrouter returned attempts-exhausted without halt. Test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestDeadRunLadder::test_a17_a_dead_run_on_the_failover_seat_halts_after_an_earlier_unusable_output failed without the change (KeyError 'halt') and passes with it; a mutant restoring the all-failures check was observed to fail only this test. Fix: exhausted() grants halt guidance when the last failure on every route (transport, model) was a transport error or a dead run. harvest.md's halt sentence was replaced to state the same condition. Commit 75bb090c.

findings.claim: No test independently pins the re-review tier for a later full read. Reverting security to frontier during a round-2 sweep could pass while dispatching the wrong model. Assert the expected tier from the roster and round number before checking its pin.
findings.reason: Confirmed the gap: a mutant making a sweep round dispatch every lens at its declared tier passed all 219 emitter tests. emit_prompts_test.py::TestSeatPins::test_a9_the_round_record_names_each_lens_pin now asserts each entry's tier_this_round against the roster (declared tier in round one, re_review_tier or declared tier later) before checking the pin. Against the mutant it fails for prose-sweep, spec-sweep and typed-code-sweep; against the branch it passes. Test-only change. Commit 7774cae8.

findings.claim: The doctrine evaluation uses readers with additional context, so its passing answers do not establish that the named files alone determine the dispatch. Repeat the twenty-seven scenarios with the required isolated inputs.
findings.reason: Re-ran all 27 A13 reads on isolated readers: headless claude -p --model sonnet in an empty directory with --setting-sources "", a replaced --system-prompt, --tools Read,Grep,Glob and only copies of the five named files (from 7774cae8) reachable via --add-dir. Isolation trial: the isolated reader reports only the userEmail and Environment blocks and three tools; a control run with default settings reports ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules/delegation.md, plugin context and MCP tools. Result 27 of 27 keyed answers, no self-corrections, no revision needed. Recorded in /Users/scott/grilling-corpus/2026-10-04-pin-408/scenarios/results-3.md with raw outputs in scenarios/results-3-raw/. The sentence in evals/dispatch-scenarios.md that said 'a fresh native subagent' was replaced to name the isolated reader and why an Agent-tool subagent does not qualify. Commit 6643c534. No unit test in the suite exercises a doctrine evaluation; the check that decides this finding is A13's own protocol. Failing observation: scenarios/results-2.md, readers that inherited the global instruction files and the memory index (one quoted the index). Passing observation: scenarios/results-3.md, 27 of 27 reads on headless `claude -p --model sonnet` readers with `--setting-sources ""`, a replaced system prompt and only the five named files reachable, after an isolation trial showed such a reader sees no instruction file while a default reader sees CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules and plugin context.

findings.claim: change_diffs recomputes and buffers the same diff separately for every lens sharing a revision pair. Reusing the computed bytes per pair would preserve every required file and refusal behavior while eliminating repeated Git work and duplicate memory.
findings.reason: Reproduced: an instrumented subprocess.run saw 5 git diff calls for a round-one typed-code emission. Test emit_prompts_test.py::TestChangeFile::test_a18_lenses_sharing_a_revision_pair_share_one_diff failed without the change (assert 5 == 1) and passes with it. Fix: change_diffs computes each distinct start revision once and reuses its bytes; the A18 file-content, empty-change and unknown-revision tests still pass. Commit cdd53cc1.

findings.claim: The round-1 failover example uses effort high, contradicting the full-scope OpenRouter pin. A dispatcher following the example dispatches at the wrong effort.
findings.reason: Confirmed: the round-1 correctness failover seat is openrouter/frontier/full, whose pin in contracts.json is effort low. In harvest.md's transport-error example the line '--transport openrouter --model <model> --effort high \' was replaced with '--effort low'. Commit a55b0e4d. No test exercises an example command in harvest.md; the check is the replaced sentence read against the pin: the round-1 failover example now says `--effort low`, which is contracts.json's pin for the openrouter/frontier/full seat (A6's test_a6_every_lens_pin_has_its_stated_effort pins that value; the example's agreement with it was verified by reading).

findings.claim: The doctrine says every refusal ends the lens, although an off-ladder refusal permits a corrected claim. Following this instruction abandons a recoverable lens and leaves the round incomplete.
findings.reason: Confirmed: off-ladder and malformed-flag refusals are raised before any ledger write and spend no attempt (dispatch_gate.py claim(); test_a_refused_claim_rewrites_nothing_and_grants_no_attempt). In harvest.md, 'A refusal (exit 2) ends that lens.' was replaced with 'An `attempts-exhausted` refusal (exit 2) ends that lens. A claim refused as `off-ladder`, or for a missing or malformed flag, spends no attempt: correct it and claim again.', and 'Any other refusal closes that lens alone' with 'Any other `attempts-exhausted` refusal closes that lens alone'. Commit a55b0e4d.

findings.claim: The empty-output guidance asserts that the reviewer never ran and directs a transport-error recovery. A watchdog-ended dead run can also leave no output, so this guidance sends the dispatcher past the required effort step-down.
findings.reason: Confirmed: a watchdog kill for silence leaves the claimed output empty and is a dead run. In harvest.md 'The reviewer never ran.' was replaced with 'An attempt your watchdog killed for silence leaves nothing too, and it is a dead run.' The gate's no-output message, which said the reviewer never ran and named only transport-error, was replaced to name dead-run with the kill line for a watchdog kill and transport-error with the route's error otherwise. Test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestIngest::test_a_claimed_path_holding_no_file_is_a_transport_failure gained an assertion that the message names dead-run; it failed without the change and passes with it. Commit 837f8a4c.

findings.claim: The recovery comment still recommends another model on the same transport when one model is saturated. That rationale contradicts the pinned failover decision and suggests a free-hand model substitution.
findings.reason: The MAX_ATTEMPTS comment's sentences 'because a model can sit at capacity for the length of a round while another model of the same vendor answers: a single transport flip abandons a live vendor on one saturated model's say-so' were replaced with 'Every attempt declares transport AND model, so the ledger names the route each attempt ran on and the routes a halt reports as exhausted.' The same rationale in check_route's docstring ('a dead vendor and a saturated model recover in opposite directions') was removed. Commit a55b0e4d. No test exercises a code comment; the check is the comment read against the doctrine: the MAX_ATTEMPTS comment and check_route's docstring no longer argue for a same-vendor model swap, and the only recovery they describe is the failover seat the routing table fixes, which is what harvest.md and A13's scenarios 2 and 3 require.

findings.claim: The exhausted helper's docstring still limits halt guidance to transport-class failures. It misstates the helper's current behavior for dead runs.
findings.reason: exhausted()'s docstring first line 'carrying halt guidance when every recorded failure was transport-class' was replaced with 'carrying halt guidance when the last failure on every route the lens ran on was a transport error or a dead run', matching both ROUTE_FAILURES and the per-route rule the correctness.r1.f2 fix introduced. Commit 75bb090c. No test exercises a docstring; the check is the docstring read against the implementation it describes: exhausted()'s docstring now states the per-route last-failure rule that test_a17_a_dead_run_on_the_failover_seat_halts_after_an_earlier_unusable_output pins in dispatch_gate_test.py.

findings.claim: The gate accepts any different transport string as failover. After an initial Codex attempt, a dead-run claim with --transport openai is authorized and spends an attempt despite naming no valid failover seat. A subsequent claim for the actual OpenRouter failover is then refused as exhausted and halts the round.
findings.reason: Reproduced: before the fix, test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestDeadRunLadder::test_a17_a_transport_that_is_not_the_failover_seat_is_refused (initial codex/gpt-5.6-terra/high, then dead-run --transport openai --effort low) failed because the gate returned exit 0 with authorized=true at attempt 2. Fix: check_ladder now accepts a failover only onto FAILOVER_TRANSPORT[start] (codex<->openrouter), and the step-down branch also requires the starting transport, so any third transport is refused off-ladder and spends nothing. With the fix the test passes (observed both). A mutant dropping the same-transport guard from the step-down branch also fails this test. Commit 56130d01.

findings.claim: The tests do not pin exhaustion when a dead-run claim tries to return to the starting transport after failover. A regression could return off-ladder without halt guidance, telling the dispatcher to correct and retry an exhausted lens. Parameterize the post-failover test over both requested transports.
findings.reason: The test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestDeadRunLadder::test_a17_a_dead_run_after_the_failover_is_out_of_attempts is now parameterized over the requested transport (failover-transport: openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3/low; starting-transport: codex/gpt-5.6-terra/medium) crossed with failover on attempt 2 and 3. Against the reviewer's mutant (history condition guarded by transport != start) the [2-starting-transport] and [3-starting-transport] cases failed and the other two passed; against the unmutated gate all four pass (observed both). Commit 56130d01.

findings.claim: The ROUTE_FAILURES comment implies that an earlier unusable output prevents the round from halting. The current rule considers each route's last failure, so a route that produced unusable output and then died can still trigger a halt.
findings.reason: Replaced the ROUTE_FAILURES comment sentence 'A lens that runs out of attempts on these alone halts the round; a reviewer that produced garbage does not.' with 'A lens that runs out of attempts halts the round when the last failure on every route it ran on is one of these.', matching exhausted(). No test exercises a comment; the behaviour it describes stays pinned by test dispatch_gate_test.py::TestDeadRunLadder::test_a17_a_dead_run_on_the_failover_seat_halts_after_an_earlier_unusable_output. Commit e399db1d.

findings.claim: The refusal rules prescribe both retrying and halting after an off-ladder claim following a dead run.
findings.reason: Verified: dispatch_gate.py attaches halt guidance only through exhausted(), whose code is attempts-exhausted; an off-ladder refusal is raised without a halt block. harvest.md 'When the gate refuses' replaced 'A refusal carries halt guidance when the last failure on every route the lens ran on was a dead route or a dead run.' with 'An `attempts-exhausted` refusal carries halt guidance when the last failure on every route the lens ran on was a dead route or a dead run.' The off-ladder/malformed-flag sentence in 'Every dispatch is claimed first' (spends no attempt, correct it and claim again) is unchanged, so each case has one sentence and they no longer overlap. Commit 78c49400. No test exercises prose.

findings.claim: A watchdog-ended attempt that leaves no output file receives conflicting failure classifications.
findings.reason: Same defect as global-consistency.r1.f1, fixed once. harvest.md 'Reading a lens report' replaced 'A claimed path holding no file at all is refused as a transport failure, not a reviewer one: the route wrote nothing.' with 'A claimed path holding nothing is refused as `no-output`, because the attempt wrote nothing. Claim again with reason `dead-run` and the kill line as the evidence when your watchdog killed it for silence, and with reason `transport-error` and the route's error otherwise.', which restates the gate's no-output refusal message in dispatch_gate.py and agrees with the dead-run section. Commit 0fd61251. Net growth two lines. No test exercises prose.

findings.claim: The surviving sentence in 'Reading a lens report' still tells the dispatcher that a claimed output path holding no file 'is refused as a transport failure, not a reviewer one: the route wrote nothing', while the change's own updated doctrine says a watchdog-killed attempt also leaves no file and is a dead run, and the gate's rewritten no-output refusal message now directs a dead-run claim first and a transport-error claim only otherwise. A dispatcher following the stale sentence claims transport-error where the new doctrine requires dead-run.
findings.reason: Same defect as internal-consistency.r1.f2, fixed once in commit 0fd61251: the stale sentence classifying every empty claimed path as a transport failure was replaced by the gate's no-output guidance (dead-run with the kill line after a watchdog kill for silence, transport-error with the route's error otherwise). No test exercises prose.

findings.claim: The committed eval protocol in evals/dispatch-scenarios.md prescribes a headless 'claude -p --model sonnet' invocation and explicitly disqualifies the Agent tool ('An Agent-tool subagent is not, because it inherits the global instruction files and the memory index'), while the acceptance criterion that authorizes the scenarios specifies 'a fresh native subagent'. In this repository's vocabulary ('The native Agent tool and Workflow are the default substrate', src/user/.claude/rules/delegation.md), a native subagent is an Agent-tool subagent, so the committed protocol narrows the criterion's reader to a different mechanism without the criterion saying so.
findings.reason: Deferred: the criterion's phrase 'fresh native subagent' and the committed protocol's headless reader will be aligned when the criteria are next restated. Neither the criteria file nor the protocol is edited in this round.

findings.claim: evals/dispatch-scenarios.md ships inside the review-panel skill directory, which the installer copies as-is into ~/.claude/skills/, and it instructs its reader to load files by repository-relative source paths ('src/user/.claude/skills/review-panel/harvest.md', 'src/user/.claude/skills/choosing-a-delegate/references/model-routing.md', 'as paths from the repository root'). Deployed beside the skill in a user home or used from another project, those paths resolve to nothing, which is exactly the dead-end citation the deployed-prose rule exists to prevent.
findings.reason: Advisory fixed because it is cheap and right. evals/dispatch-scenarios.md replaced the repository-relative list ('The files every scenario gives, as paths from the repository root:' and three src/user/... paths) with 'The files every scenario gives:' naming this skill's `harvest.md`, this skill's `contracts.json` and the `choosing-a-delegate` skill's `references/model-routing.md`, and replaced each scenario's 'Round record: `src/user/.claude/skills/review-panel/evals/round-N-typed-code.json`' with 'Round record: `round-N-typed-code.json` beside this file'. Keyed answers unchanged. Commit 5bc9e856. No test exercises prose.

findings.claim: The gate's halt guidance and harvest.md now fire the halt when the last failure on every route was a dead run as well as a transport error, but the review-verdict schema offers only 'transport-failure' as the halt reason for route deaths and defines it as 'A transport failure' where 'a dispatch died on its route'. A halt caused purely by dead runs (the ladder's terminal case) must now be recorded under a reason whose definition excludes the failure that caused it, and neither the schema nor the change notes the stretch.
findings.reason: Deferred: the review-verdict schema lives in another skill and is outside this change; the halt-reason vocabulary (no reason naming a dead-run halt) is noted for a follow-on item. The schema is not edited.

findings.claim: The introduction narrates past improvisation that the deployed reader cannot resolve. Keep the current rationale about auditability and remove the episode.
findings.reason: harvest.md introduction replaced 'Every rule here exists because a round hit the case and the invoker had to improvise; an improvised rule is one nobody can audit afterwards.' with 'Each rule settles a case the invoker would otherwise improvise, and an improvised rule is one nobody can audit afterwards.' The episode is gone and the auditability rationale stays. Commit e43ccecc. No test exercises prose.

findings.claim: The transport section narrates past outages without a resolvable reference. The present-tense rationale for symmetric failover can stand independently.
findings.reason: harvest.md 'Transport is symmetric' replaced 'Neither direction is the exceptional one, and neither transport is the more reliable one — both have been down while the other worked.' with 'Neither direction is the exceptional one, because either transport can be down while the other works.' The narrated outages are gone and the symmetric-failover rationale stays in one sentence. Commit e43ccecc. No test exercises prose.

commit.subject: feat(review-panel): pin reviewer effort and tools as data and bound a dying run's recovery [9k9.408]
commit.why: The agent running a review round chose each reviewer's effort and tool access itself, and avoided one model for whole-document reads on a belief no run record supported. Review cost and coverage were unpredictable.
commit.change: The panel's configuration holds effort and tools for every reviewer slot, and each round records what it used. Every reviewer receives the change as a diff file. A run that dies mid-reasoning retries one effort step lower, then on the other provider, then halts the round. Models still come from the shared routing table.
commit.verification: make ci, doc-lint and content-lint exit 0 at 5bc9e856. 27 of 27 isolated doctrine reads matched the key. Code and prose review circuits both reached a clean sweep. The gate does not yet check a run used its pinned effort.
